bankAlignment.source: Cached OS London five-foot 1893 map and reviewed Bow/Magnet supplied building outlines

Opposite bank and remaining channel vertices retained; local map reconciliation, not a surveyed shoreline. The final control also moves 2.04 m north to keep the tidal/retained channel junction disjoint.

bankAlignment.evidence: Two works-side controls clear the restored western furnace range. Vertex 39 follows the prior Bow Bridge correction; the opposite bank is retained.

neighbourhood.registration: First-pass registration using the rounded NLS WGS84 sheet bounds and manually read neatlines, then projection to EPSG:27700. Relative traces are map-based; absolute placement may be tens of metres out. Not a surveyed or control-point-fitted georeference.

housingExclusions.name: Railway goods and coal yard interior

sewer.evidence: Centreline read from OS VIII.32 and the supplied mosaic; translated to meet the existing listed bridge anchor. Height follows author guidance of roughly roof level. Beyond inspected coverage the two ends continue along their end bearings for skyline continuity; those extensions are inferred, not surveyed.
sewer.alignmentEvidence: Western centreline replaces the straight 1400 m extrapolation. High Street crosses above the enclosed sewer, not below an exposed walkway. Exact nineteenth-century section still unresolved.
sewer.bankEndsEvidence: Bank ends follow the drawn water edge, set back 1.5 m, and the 6 m railway corridor. The position of each end is derived from the mapped channel and railway; the brick end wall, its 0.8 m thickness and its footing are interpreted, not a surveyed abutment.

garden.evidence: Author identifies allotments in the 1900 south photograph. The author-dated 1945 aerial informs landscape scale and patchwork only. Continuity of the broader extent into c1900 is inferred; individual beds, planting and sheds are interpreted. Earlier river courses retained; Prescott Cut excluded.
garden.layoutEvidence: Inferred plot divisions and planting, aligned with the mapped field edge. Varied sizes and shared access gaps are visual interpretations, not traced household boundaries.

mill.evidence: OS VIII.32 names Abbey Mill (Corn); Main southern mill mass re-anchored to OS VIII.32 pixel (1090,625) at 1800 px width, clear of the mapped lane crossing; author suggests the c1800 mill building form probably continued into c1900, analogous to nearby Three Mills. studyChimneys.evidence: One deliberately simple chimney per chosen site, placed at the range centre; sites with individually registered ranges omit it. Heights and radii are study assumptions, not surveyed stacks.
